articles.title: Letter: The Streetlight Upgrade on Adams Place Needs Attention
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the November meeting. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

To the editor: I have lived on Adams Place for 40 years, and I want to say what a difference the Upper Commons Historical Society has made. Please keep the streetlight upgrade in the budget. Many of us on Adams Place use it every week.
Sergio Pelletier, Foxglove Heights

articles.deck: The program begins in February and is open to all students in grade 4 and up.
body: Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for February. Students will meet on Saturday afternoons in the Bellwood Chapel, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.
The board will review the results at the end of the summer term.
Principal Sergio Dunmore said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers. Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for February.

articles.title: Theodore Bruckner, 80, Neighborhood Baker
articles.deck: Friends remember Theodore Bruckner for the many years of service to Foundry Row.
body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Upper Commons Historical Society in his or her name.

Born in Foundry Row in the years after the war, Theodore Bruckner spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Foundry Row.

body: Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height. Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal.
